text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Finno-Ugrian folk festival is keeping away from busy capital city Tallinn and is having concerts in the countryside.
- With the first stage of the Baltic Challenge military exercise over, 1,000 men from the United States troops will have a day off to visit Tallinn.
- The rise of the Talse index on the stock exchange to a record 322.86 points was probably caused by the European Commission's decision on membership talks, analysts said.
- The Russian embassy in Tallinn does not see any danger to Russian security from the Baltic Challenge exercise as one Russian newspaper said.
- Neither the Estonian nor Ukrainian educational systems are ready for opening a Ukrainian school in Estonia.
- Competitions for teams of rescue workers in Iceland between July 19-29 will be a test for the Estonian team, formed only recently.
- Estonian Linnart Mall is one of the candidates for the post of secretary general of the Unrepresented Nations Organisation, holding a meeting in south Estonia.
- U.S. NRG Energy, part of Northern States Power, does not intend to change its business plan for the Narva power stations despite the disapproval of a commission of experts.

- Agricultural producers gained a promise of an additional 100 million kroons from next year's state budget in talks with the government with another 100 million kroons after a law on markets is adopted.
